title: Call Center checkout durably recovers an ambiguous request while cashier checkout retains it only in memory
scope: Targeted comparison of restart recovery for checkout idempotency requests across the two active WinUI stations; follows the request through client store, VM dispatch, and server replay lookup. It does not certify all station lifecycle or deployed usage.

behavior.call_center: App configures FileRetainedRequestStore before view models. CallCenterViewModel constructor restores owner-scoped CheckoutOrderRequest, and SendCheckoutAsync saves before network dispatch; unknown outcomes preserve it for same-request retry, successful or definite rejected outcomes clear it.
behavior.cashier: App also configures FileRetainedRequestStore and uses RetainedRequest<T> for selected other operations, but checkout uses private CurrentCheckoutRequestId and _pendingCheckout fields. Same-process unknown outcomes reuse the request. This checkout code does not persist or restore the pending CheckoutOrderRequest across process reconstruction.
behavior.server: CheckoutOrderHandler.HandleAsync looks up CheckoutRequestId before doing work and returns the existing order on replay. The key helps only if the client retains the original request/key.
behavior.consequence: After a cashier process/power loss during an unknown checkout result, the client-side exact request is not recovered through the inspected checkout path. A later reconstructed order can carry a fresh request id and represent a second order. This is a conditional duplicate-intent/recovery risk, not proof of automatic retry, duplicate database write, or real-world occurrence. UI-001 already covers cashier checkout and related money operations; this comparison adds the cross-station contrast and is not a new finding.

counterevidence_and_limits: Cashier's same-process retry retains the immutable DTO and server idempotency key.
Call Center's startup restore can expose the same original checkout DTO after process loss.
The source does not establish that an operator will recreate the same order, nor that any duplicate order occurred.
No runtime/power-loss/network-fault test was performed; actual deployment and operator workflow are unverified.
This comparison does not independently re-review all UI-001 surfaces; it references that existing finding rather than duplicating it.
recommendation: For future remediation, align cashier checkout with a durable owner-scoped retained request already used by the Call Center and other operations. Save the immutable request before dispatch, restore and reconcile it before allowing a new order, and clear only after a definite rejection or confirmed success. Avoid persisting credentials or unrelated cart state. Add fresh-view-model recovery tests for committed-but-lost response and definite rejection; verify same request id results in one order and one set of side effects in an isolated integration database.

needed: Construct a fresh CashierViewModel with an unresolved retained checkout and assert the original DTO/key is available before new checkout.
Simulate server commit followed by lost response; restart client; retry exact DTO and assert one order, one inventory deduction, one financial journal entry and one intended print job.
Simulate definite server rejection; verify correction path does not preserve an invalid request indefinitely.
Compare cashier and Call Center process-loss recovery behavior using the same fake retained store and API outcomes.

source_references.evidence: The application initializes a station-scoped file retained-request store before view-model construction.
The view-model constructor calls RecoverPendingOperations during desk construction.

Call Center stores the immutable request before dispatch, restores it under the owner key at startup, and retries that same DTO; a definite first rejection clears it, while unknown results preserve it.
Cashier also configures the file store, proving storage is available to the app; this does not by itself persist checkout DTOs.

Cashier checkout keeps its request ID and unresolved DTO only in view-model fields. CompleteCheckoutAsync sets _pendingCheckout before dispatch and reuses it in the same process, but no RetainedRequestStore Save/Load is used by this checkout path.
The server returns the prior order for the same CheckoutRequestId; losing the client copy after commit can prevent that same-key replay path from being used by a restarted client.
